s: a male given name from English
Arthur.et: Borrowed from English in the 18th century.

s: Und so begann eine Art von Beziehung.
And so began a kind of relationship.
That's not his way [of doing things].
Art.et: From Middle High German art, from Old High German *art, from Proto-West Germanic *ard, from Proto-Germanic *ardiz.

s: one who performs physical tricks in a circus or similar context, e.g. a wirewalker, trapezist, or juggler
Der Sekt ward süßer, Unrat immer glücklicher. Zu seiner nächsten Nummer schritt der Artist auf den Händen hinaus und erwarb ungemessenen Beifall.
Artist.et: Early 14th century, borrowed from Medieval Latin artista (“artist”). The modern meaning “circus player” developed in the 19th century under influence from French artiste.

s: Inspiriert sind sie von Artists wie Partiboi69 oder MCR-T. „Ich war mir sicher, dass es funktionieren wird, weil es eine Lücke gab: Vocals mit Party-Mucke von einer Bad-Bitch-FLINTA-Artist“, so Kat.
Artist.et: Borrowed from English artist, used as a gender-neutral umbrella term.

s: a male given name, variant of Arthur
artichoke (edible plant related to the thistle)
Artischocke.et: From Northern Italian articiocco, from Provençal archichaut, arquichaut, from Old Spanish alcarchofa, from Andalusian Arabic خرشوف (ḵaršūf), from Arabic الْخُرْشُوف (al-ḵuršūf), definite form of خُرْشُوف (ḵuršūf).

Artikel.et: From Middle High German artikel, from Latin articulus.

Art und Weise.et: Pleonastic combination of Art + Weise, which both mean the same thing even on their own.
